raw: Act 3, Scene 3 — Friar Lawrence’s cell
Enter Friar Lawrence.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Romeo, come forth; come forth, thou fearful man.
Affliction is enanmour’d of thy parts
And thou art wedded to calamity.

sentences.en: Romeo, come forward.
Come forward, you fearful man.
Trouble has fallen in love with you.
You are married to disaster.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Father, what news? What is the Prince’s doom?
What sorrow craves acquaintance at my hand,
That I yet know not?

sentences.en: Father, what is the news?
What is the Prince's sentence?
What new sorrow wants to meet me that I do not know yet?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Too familiar
Is my dear son with such sour company.
I bring thee tidings of the Prince’s doom.

sentences.en: My dear son is too close with such bad company.
I bring you news of the Prince's sentence.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What less than doomsday is the Prince’s doom?

sentences.en: Is the Prince's sentence anything less than death?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
A gentler judgment vanish’d from his lips,
Not body’s death, but body’s banishment.

sentences.en: He gave a gentler sentence.
It is not death of the body.
It is only banishment of the body.

speaker: ROMEO

sentences.en: Ha, banishment?
Be kind and say death.
Exile looks much more terrifying than death.
Do not say banishment.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hence from Verona art thou banished.
Be patient, for the world is broad and wide.

sentences.en: You are banished from Verona.
Be patient, for the world is broad and wide.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
There is no world without Verona walls,
But purgatory, torture, hell itself.
Hence banished is banish’d from the world,
And world’s exile is death. Then banished
Is death misterm’d. Calling death banished,
Thou cutt’st my head off with a golden axe,
And smilest upon the stroke that murders me.

sentences.en: There is no world outside the walls of Verona.
It is only purgatory, torture, and hell itself.
To be banished is to be removed from the world.
And exile from the world is death.
Then banishment is just another word for death.
By calling death 'banished', you cut off my head with a golden axe.
You smile at the strike that kills me.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
O deadly sin, O rude unthankfulness!
Thy fault our law calls death, but the kind Prince,
Taking thy part, hath brush’d aside the law,
And turn’d that black word death to banishment.
This is dear mercy, and thou see’st it not.

sentences.en: Oh, what a deadly sin!
You are so ungrateful!
Our law calls your crime death.
But the kind Prince takes your side.
He ignored the law.
He changed that dark word 'death' to 'banishment'.
This is a great mercy.
You do not see it.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
’Tis torture, and not mercy. Heaven is here
Where Juliet lives, and every cat and dog,
And little mouse, every unworthy thing,
Live here in heaven and may look on her,
But Romeo may not. More validity,
More honourable state, more courtship lives
In carrion flies than Romeo. They may seize
On the white wonder of dear Juliet’s hand,
And steal immortal blessing from her lips,
Who, even in pure and vestal modesty
Still blush, as thinking their own kisses sin.
But Romeo may not, he is banished.
This may flies do, when I from this must fly.
They are free men but I am banished.
And say’st thou yet that exile is not death?
Hadst thou no poison mix’d, no sharp-ground knife,
No sudden mean of death, though ne’er so mean,
But banished to kill me? Banished?
O Friar, the damned use that word in hell.
Howling attends it. How hast thou the heart,
Being a divine, a ghostly confessor,
A sin-absolver, and my friend profess’d,
To mangle me with that word banished?

sentences.en: It is torture, not mercy.
Heaven is here where Juliet lives, and every cat and dog lives here in heaven.
Every little mouse and every unworthy thing lives here in heaven.
They can all look at her, but Romeo cannot.
Even the flies on dead meat have more worth, more honor, and more chance to court her than Romeo.
They can grab the white wonder of Juliet's hand.
They can steal an immortal blessing from her lips.
Her lips are so pure that they still blush because they think even touching each other is a sin.
But Romeo cannot do this because he is banished.
Flies can do this, while I must fly away.
They are free, but I am banished.
Do you still say that exile is not death?
Did you have no poison, no sharp knife, or no quick way to kill me except 'banished'?
Banished?
Oh Friar, the damned souls in hell use that word.
Howling follows that word.
How can you have such a heart?
You are a holy man and a spiritual priest.
You are a person who forgives sins.
You are my declared friend.
How can you hurt me with that word 'banished'?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Thou fond mad man, hear me speak a little,

sentences.en: You foolish mad man, listen to me speak for a moment.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O, thou wilt speak again of banishment.

sentences.en: Oh, you will speak of banishment again.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
I’ll give thee armour to keep off that word,
Adversity’s sweet milk, philosophy,
To comfort thee, though thou art banished.

sentences.en: I will give you armor to protect you from that word.
Philosophy is the sweet milk of hard times.
It will comfort you, even though you are banished.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Yet banished? Hang up philosophy.
Unless philosophy can make a Juliet,
Displant a town, reverse a Prince’s doom,
It helps not, it prevails not, talk no more.

sentences.en: Still banished?
Stop talking about philosophy.
Unless philosophy can create a Juliet, or move a town, or change a Prince's judgment, it does not help.
It does not work.
Do not talk about it anymore.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: O, then I see that mad men have no ears.

sentences.en: Oh, I see that mad men have no ears.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: How should they, when that wise men have no eyes?

sentences.en: How could they, when wise men have no eyes?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Let me dispute with thee of thy estate.

sentences.en: Let me argue with you about your situation.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Thou canst not speak of that thou dost not feel.
Wert thou as young as I, Juliet thy love,
An hour but married, Tybalt murdered,
Doting like me, and like me banished,
Then mightst thou speak, then mightst thou tear thy hair,
And fall upon the ground as I do now,
Taking the measure of an unmade grave.

sentences.en: You cannot speak of what you do not feel.
Imagine that you were as young as I and Juliet was your love.
Imagine you had been married for only one hour and Tybalt was murdered.
Imagine you were obsessed with her like me and also sent away forever by law.
Then you could speak about it, pull your hair out, and fall to the ground like I am doing now.
You would be measuring your own grave.

raw: Knocking within.

sentences.en: Someone knocks at the door.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Arise; one knocks. Good Romeo, hide thyself.

sentences.en: Get up. Someone is knocking. Good Romeo, hide yourself.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Not I, unless the breath of heartsick groans
Mist-like infold me from the search of eyes.

sentences.en: I will not.
Unless the breath of sad groans covers me like mist from the eyes of others.

raw: Knocking.

sentences.en: Someone knocks.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hark, how they knock!—Who’s there?—Romeo, arise,
Thou wilt be taken.—Stay awhile.—Stand up.

sentences.en: Listen, how they knock! Who is there?
Romeo, get up. You will be caught.
Wait a moment. Stand up.

raw: Knocking.

sentences.en: Someone knocks.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Run to my study.—By-and-by.—God’s will,
What simpleness is this.—I come, I come.

sentences.en: Run to my study.
I am coming.
Good God, how foolish you are being!
I am coming.

raw: Knocking.

sentences.en: Someone knocks.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Who knocks so hard? Whence come you, what’s your will?

sentences.en: Who knocks so hard? Where do you come from and what is your purpose?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Let me come in, and you shall know my errand.
I come from Lady Juliet.

sentences.en: Let me come in so that you will know my reason.
I come from Lady Juliet.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Welcome then.

sentences.en: Welcome then.

raw: Enter Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O holy Friar, O, tell me, holy Friar,
Where is my lady’s lord, where’s Romeo?

sentences.en: O holy Friar, tell me, holy Friar, where is my lady's lord?
Where is Romeo?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: There on the ground, with his own tears made drunk.

sentences.en: He is there on the ground.
He is drunk from his own tears.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O, he is even in my mistress’ case.
Just in her case! O woeful sympathy!
Piteous predicament. Even so lies she,
Blubbering and weeping, weeping and blubbering.
Stand up, stand up; stand, and you be a man.
For Juliet’s sake, for her sake, rise and stand.
Why should you fall into so deep an O?

sentences.en: Oh, he is in the same state as my young lady.
He is exactly in her situation!
What a sad sympathy and a pitiful situation.
She is just like that, crying and sobbing.
She is crying and blubbering.
Stand up and be a man.
For Juliet's sake, for her sake, rise and stand.
Why fall into such deep despair?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Nurse.

sentences.en: Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Ah sir, ah sir, death’s the end of all.

sentences.en: Oh sir, death ends everything.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Spakest thou of Juliet? How is it with her?
Doth not she think me an old murderer,
Now I have stain’d the childhood of our joy
With blood remov’d but little from her own?
Where is she? And how doth she? And what says
My conceal’d lady to our cancell’d love?

sentences.en: Are you talking about Juliet?
How is she doing?
Does she think I am a murderer?
I have stained our young joy with blood from her own family.
Where is she?
How is she feeling?
What does my secret wife say about our ruined love?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O, she says nothing, sir, but weeps and weeps;
And now falls on her bed, and then starts up,
And Tybalt calls, and then on Romeo cries,
And then down falls again.

sentences.en: She says nothing, sir, but she only cries and cries.
Now she falls on her bed and then gets up.
She calls out 'Tybalt' and then cries out for Romeo.
Then she falls down again.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
As if that name,
Shot from the deadly level of a gun,
Did murder her, as that name’s cursed hand
Murder’d her kinsman. O, tell me, Friar, tell me,
In what vile part of this anatomy
Doth my name lodge? Tell me, that I may sack
The hateful mansion.

sentences.en: It is as if that name hit her like a bullet from a gun.
That name killed her, just as its cursed hand killed her relative.
Tell me, Friar.
Tell me where my name stays in this body.
Tell me so I can remove that hateful part.

raw: Drawing his sword.

sentences.en: Romeo draws his sword.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold thy desperate hand.
Art thou a man? Thy form cries out thou art.
Thy tears are womanish, thy wild acts denote
The unreasonable fury of a beast.
Unseemly woman in a seeming man,
And ill-beseeming beast in seeming both!
Thou hast amaz’d me. By my holy order,
I thought thy disposition better temper’d.
Hast thou slain Tybalt? Wilt thou slay thyself?
And slay thy lady, that in thy life lives,
By doing damned hate upon thyself?
Why rail’st thou on thy birth, the heaven and earth?
Since birth, and heaven and earth, all three do meet
In thee at once; which thou at once wouldst lose.
Fie, fie, thou sham’st thy shape, thy love, thy wit,
Which, like a usurer, abound’st in all,
And usest none in that true use indeed
Which should bedeck thy shape, thy love, thy wit.
Thy noble shape is but a form of wax,
Digressing from the valour of a man;
Thy dear love sworn but hollow perjury,
Killing that love which thou hast vow’d to cherish;
Thy wit, that ornament to shape and love,
Misshapen in the conduct of them both,
Like powder in a skilless soldier’s flask,
Is set afire by thine own ignorance,
And thou dismember’d with thine own defence.
What, rouse thee, man. Thy Juliet is alive,
For whose dear sake thou wast but lately dead.
There art thou happy. Tybalt would kill thee,
But thou slew’st Tybalt; there art thou happy.
The law that threaten’d death becomes thy friend,
And turns it to exile; there art thou happy.
A pack of blessings light upon thy back;
Happiness courts thee in her best array;
But like a misshaped and sullen wench,
Thou putt’st up thy Fortune and thy love.
Take heed, take heed, for such die miserable.
Go, get thee to thy love as was decreed,
Ascend her chamber, hence and comfort her.
But look thou stay not till the watch be set,
For then thou canst not pass to Mantua;
Where thou shalt live till we can find a time
To blaze your marriage, reconcile your friends,
Beg pardon of the Prince, and call thee back
With twenty hundred thousand times more joy
Than thou went’st forth in lamentation.
Go before, Nurse. Commend me to thy lady,
And bid her hasten all the house to bed,
Which heavy sorrow makes them apt unto.
Romeo is coming.

sentences.en: Stop your desperate hand.
Are you a man?
Your body looks like a man's, but your tears are like a woman's.
Your wild actions show the anger of a beast.
You look like an shameful woman in a man's body.
You look like a bad beast in both forms!
You have shocked me because I thought you had a calmer nature.
Did you kill Tybalt?
Do you want to kill yourself?
And would you kill your lady who is the life of your life?
Would you do such a hateful thing to yourself?
Why are you complaining about your birth, heaven, and earth?
Birth, heaven, and earth all meet in you at once.
You would lose all three at once.
Shame on you!
You shame your body, your love, and your mind.
Like a greedy moneylender, you have plenty of all three.
But you do not use them correctly.
Your noble body is just a form of wax.
It does not show the strength of a man.
Your dear love is just a hollow lie.
It kills the love that you promised to protect.
Your intelligence should be a decoration for your body and love.
But it is shaped wrongly in how you act.
It is like powder in an unskilled soldier's flask.
It is set on fire by your own ignorance.
And you are hurt by your own defense.
Wake up, man.
Your Juliet is alive.
Just now you wanted to die for her sake.
You are lucky there.
Tybalt would kill you, but you killed Tybalt.
You are lucky there.
The law that threatened death changed it to exile.
You are lucky there.
Many blessings are on your back.
Happiness is courting you in her best clothes.
But like a sulky, bad-tempered girl, you push away your luck and love.
Be careful.
People who do this die miserably.
Go to your love as was planned.
Go up to her room.
Go there now and comfort her.
But do not stay until the guards are set.
Then you cannot go to Mantua.
You will live there until we find a time.
We will announce your marriage.
We will make your friends agree again.
We will ask for forgiveness from the Prince.
We will bring you back with much more joy than when you left in sadness.
Go now, Nurse.
Give my regards to your lady.
Tell her to hurry everyone in the house to bed.
They are tired from their sad feelings.
Romeo is coming.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O Lord, I could have stay’d here all the night
To hear good counsel. O, what learning is!
My lord, I’ll tell my lady you will come.

sentences.en: Oh Lord, I could have stayed here all night.
I could have heard good advice.
What great learning there is!
My lord, I will tell my lady that you are coming.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Do so, and bid my sweet prepare to chide.

sentences.en: Do that, and tell my sweet love to get ready to scold me.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Here sir, a ring she bid me give you, sir.
Hie you, make haste, for it grows very late.

sentences.en: Here is a ring she told me to give you.
Hurry, go now.
It is getting very late.

raw: Exit.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: How well my comfort is reviv’d by this.

sentences.en: This gives me great comfort.
It makes me feel better.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Go hence, good night, and here stands all your state:
Either be gone before the watch be set,
Or by the break of day disguis’d from hence.
Sojourn in Mantua. I’ll find out your man,
And he shall signify from time to time
Every good hap to you that chances here.
Give me thy hand; ’tis late; farewell; good night.

sentences.en: Go away now. Good night.
Everything depends on this.
Either leave before the guards are set, or leave at dawn in disguise.
Stay for a while in Mantua.
I will find your man.
He will tell you of every good thing that happens here.
Give me your hand.
It is late. Goodbye. Good night.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
But that a joy past joy calls out on me,
It were a grief so brief to part with thee.
Farewell.

sentences.en: If a joy greater than all joys were not calling me, it would be sad to leave you so quickly.
Goodbye.

raw: Exeunt.
